Motivation
Every release today ends with a manual upload to an S3 bucket that only Confluent can write to. The system tests then run against copies of the release that nobody verifies.
The compatibility and upgrade tests run older releases from/opt/kafka-<version>. Thetests/docker/Dockerfiledownloads them fromhttps://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/kafka-packages. Each release needs one line for its binary tarball and one for itskafka-streams-<version>-test.jar, which the streams upgrade tests load fromlibs/. Thevagrant/base.shkeeps a second copy of the same list.
After a release, theRelease Processasks the release manager to:
Updategradle/dependencies.gradle,tests/docker/Dockerfile,tests/kafkatest/version.pyandvagrant/base.sh, as in#22373and#23629.
Upload both tarballs and the test jar tokafka-packages. Confluent owns the bucket, so a release manager who does not work there has to ask a Confluent committer.
This causes three problems:
Uploads get missed.The upload is one of theAfter releasesteps in the Release Process, so a release manager may forget it.
The copies are not the released artifacts.Nothing checks a checksum or a signature. The 2.4.1 and 4.2.2 test jars on S3 hold the same classes as Maven Central but were rebuilt later, so their bytes differ.
The test setup depends on a vendor's bucket.The project cannot fix a missing or broken file without asking Confluent.

Proposed Changes
One image,ghcr.io/apache/kafka/system-test-deps, holds every release the system tests need. A workflow builds it from the official artifacts, and the ducker image copies it instead of downloading from S3.
The deps image
A new directory,tests/docker/deps/, holds aDockerfileand afetch-kafka.shscript. The Dockerfile lists one line per release:RUN fetch-kafka 4.2.2 2.13
RUN fetch-kafka 4.3.1 2.13
fetch-kafka.sh <version> <scala version>does the following:
Downloadskafka_<scala>-<version>.tgzfromhttps://archive.apache.org/dist/kafka/<version>/.
Downloadskafka-streams-<version>-test.jarfrom Maven Central.
Verifies both detached signatures againsthttps://downloads.apache.org/kafka/KEYS, asdocker/jvm/Dockerfilealready does for the release image.
Installs the release into/opt/kafka-<version>and puts the test jar into itslibs/.
The publishing workflow
A new workflow,.github/workflows/system_test_deps_image.yml, builds and pushes the image:

A release is never removed from the image while an active branch still uses it, solatestworks for every active branch
